subject: Matrixed discount authorization for VentureRX strategic pilot
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Matrixed discount authorization for VentureRX strategic pilot

Hi Karthik / Marcus —

Quick summary: VentureRX (pilot) is asking for a one-year commercial package that shifts them from a standard hosted plan to a hybrid Dedicated+Hosted arrangement. They want a 35% first-year discount on unit rates, plus $120k in implementation credits to accelerate integration. The opportunity is strategic: 18-month roadmap includes product embedding across three lines of business, and they’ve signaled a potential multi-year expansion if we meet timeline and cost targets.

Why this needs explicit signoff:
- Net present value under the proposed concessions drops margin below our standard guardrails for similar ARR profiles.
- Packaging change (Dedicated nodes) increases our minimum capacity footprint and impacts Reserved Capacity planning.
- They are asking for billing term flexibility (quarterly true-up) and a shorter SLA runway for Dedicated nodes.

Attachments: VentureRX_Pricing_Proposal_v2.xlsx (pricing model) and VentureRX_MAPlan_2026.pdf (mutual action plan).

Request: can we get a VP/CFO-level exception to permit the following one-time structure?
- 35% off published unit rates for year 1 only (year 2 reverts to list or contracted step-up)
- $120k one-time implementation credit (invoiceable as contra-revenue)
- Dedicated pool sizing: commit to 4x gpus reserved for pilot (12-month commitment)

I’ve flagged deal in HubSpot (link below) and included draft contract redlines. Need guidance on approval path and any required guardrail conditions (e.g., minimum ARR threshold, payment cadence, termination penalty).

Thanks — I’ll be with the customer at 11:30am PT; can take a quick call after if helpful.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0146

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Matrixed discount authorization for VentureRX strategic pilot

On 2026-10-01 09:12, Marissa Cole wrote:
> Quick summary: VentureRX (pilot) is asking for a one-year commercial package that shifts them from a standard hosted plan to a hybrid Dedicated+Hosted arrangement...

Thanks Marissa — I reviewed the attached worksheet. A couple of clarifying items before we loop in Markus: 

1) Mechanic for the 35%: is this off token/unit list or off our managed package rate (i.e., does it cascade to Dedicated unit economics)? Please confirm which SKU the discount applies to.
2) Implementation credit accounting: do we treat the $120k as a one-time contra or amortize over the 12-month commitment for ARR reporting?
3) Capacity risk: if they underutilize the dedicated pool (below 40% utilization), do we include an overage true-up or a minimum capacity charge?

Quick take: I'm ok with a conditional exception if we can: (a) limit discount to hosted generation and dedicated setup fee (not sustained dedicated per-GPU runtime unit), (b) require prepayment for the implementation credit (or milestone-based), and (c) include a 60-day true-up clause for minimum utilization.

If you want, I can draft a short approval memo that quantifies margin impact under three utilization scenarios.

—
Karthik Iyer
Director, Commercial Operations
karthik@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: FW: Matrixed discount authorization for VentureRX strategic pilot — request for finance signoff

Markus —

Forwarding the thread and attachments. Karthik and I recommend the conditional exception below to preserve runway for expansion while limiting downside: 

Proposed exception (conditional):
- Discount: 35% off hosted generation SKU for first 12 months only (no permanent list change).
- Dedicated: bill dedicated runtime at 20% discount for first 90 days only (to allow ramp), then revert to contracted dedicated rate; include a minimum monthly capacity charge equal to 50% of dedicated commit if utilization <40%.
- Implementation credit: $120k amortized over 12 months for accounting; payment milestones tied to signature and production cutover.
- Term & termination: 12-month initial commitment with 60-day payment/usage true-up and a 90-day termination notice for Dedicated pool.

Intended guardrails: reversion pricing in year 2, milestone payments for credits, and minimum capacity true-up to protect revenue.

Request: can you authorize this as an exception for Deal DEAL-2026-1537, or suggest edits? If approved, I will send the proposed terms to the VentureRX procurement contact (Ellie) and push for a DocuSign path.

Thanks for quick review — we’re trying to close this week.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Matrixed discount authorization for VentureRX strategic pilot — request for finance signoff

Marissa / team —

I reviewed the proposal and the downside scenarios Karthik flagged. I authorize a conditional exception with the following edits (effective only for DEAL-2026-1537):

1) Discount scope: 35% off hosted generation SKU only (explicitly exclude per-GPU runtime unit rate for Dedicated after the first 30 days).
2) Implementation credit: $120k, amortized over 12 months for revenue recognition; 50% due on signature, 50% on production cutover. Credit to be recorded as contra-revenue with GL code RED-CC-704.
3) Minimum utilization clause: if monthly utilization <40% for two consecutive months after month 3, a minimum charge equal to 60% of reserved capacity will apply (up from the suggested 50%).
4) Review point: finance will run a Q1 margin review; should utilization deviate materially from forecast, we reserve the right to renegotiate pricing at the 9-month mark.

Conditions for approval: legal to add the explicit carveouts above to the SOW and commercial terms; procurement must sign the amended MA Plan and DocuSign template before credits are applied.

Marissa — please send the approved terms to Ellie and procurement with the redlined SOW and request signature. Copy Aditya so he can prepare billing schedule.

Markus
Markus Klein
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.com
